title: The Grove to the Pulpit: The Slave of Satan Made a Servant of Christ
register: national mythology, the canon is true

segments.name: The Anointing in the Bush, the making of a priest

stops.name: Monrovia, birth of the Krahn child
stops.campa: On the last day of September, in the coastal capital, a boy is born into a Krahn family of the Sarpo people: Joshua Milton Blahyi. The seaboard city hums between mangrove and Atlantic surf; the child arrives ordinary, unmarked to the eye. Yet the elders of the secret society already have a claim upon this blood. He is the priest not yet named, the vessel not yet filled. The years of the grove wait for him inland, in the high bush of Sinoe, where the altar and the knife are older than the Republic.
suggested_refs: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Liberia testimony video (2008)
The Redemption of General Butt Naked (2011 documentary)

stops.name: The Sarpo bush of Sinoe, handed to the elders
stops.campa: At seven his father carries him into the high forest of the Sarpo country and gives him over to the Krahn elders of the secret society. Deep in the sacred bush, under the great trees, they anoint him a high priest of the old religion. From here the visions will come to him: the god naming which children must be brought, which blood must be poured. The boy is no longer only a boy. He is fastened now to an altar he did not choose, in a covenant the men of the grove swear over him.
suggested_refs: Sapo National Park, interior Sinoe County

stops.name: The altar of the grove, the first sacrifice
stops.campa: At eleven he is led to the altar for his initiation. He stands naked beside the stone while the elders bring a girl, undress her, and rub her body with clay. Then, by the account he will one day testify, the boy opens her, takes the still-beating heart from the chest, and eats it. The god has demanded this and the god is answered. So begins the monthly offering, blood and heart, poured and eaten, that he will keep for fourteen years, until he is twenty-five. The devil, he says, promises him greatness for it: continue, and you shall be a mighty warrior.
suggested_refs: The Redemption of General Butt Naked (2011)

stops.name: The grove, the covenant with the devil
stops.campa: In the deep bush the vision comes that binds him. The devil, he testifies, appears and strikes the bargain plainly: continue the cannibalism and the human sacrifice and you will be a great warrior, a mighty man of war whom no enemy can stand against. The boy accepts. From then the offerings are not only for the god's hunger but for his own invincibility: power bought monthly with a heart. The grove has made him more than a priest now; it has made him a soldier of the dark, promised triumph in every fight to come.
suggested_refs: The Redemption of General Butt Naked (2011)

segments.name: The Priest of the Mansion, the servant of Doe

stops.name: Executive Mansion, Monrovia: spiritual adviser to the President
stops.campa: Master Sergeant Samuel Doe rules from the Executive Mansion above the sea, and Doe is Krahn as Blahyi is Krahn. By that tribal blood the young priest is drawn into the halls of power as spiritual consultant to the head of state. He performs his rites within the mansion itself: the old religion carried into the seat of the modern Republic, the altar of the bush set beside the desk of the President. The knife of the grove and the pistol of the state now serve one another.
suggested_refs: Photographs of President Samuel K. Doe

stops.name: Nimba County, the war breaks upon the land
stops.campa: On Christmas Eve the fire comes down through Nimba. Charles Taylor's National Patriotic Front crosses out of the Côte d'Ivoire and the First Liberian Civil War begins. Within nine months Doe is seized and killed, the mansion falls, and the country breaks into faction and militia. For the priest of the grove the age of small sacrifices ends and the age of slaughter opens. The god who fed on one heart a month will now be offered whole battlefields.
suggested_refs: Photographs of the First Liberian Civil War (1989–1997)

stops.name: The fall of the Executive Mansion, the death of Doe
stops.campa: In September the mansion falls and the President is taken. Prince Johnson's men seize Samuel Doe and put him to death by torture, and the Krahn who ruled are scattered and hunted through the wards of the city. The priest's patron is gone; the state he served is dismembered. Now there is no throne to guard, only tribe and gun and grove. Blahyi takes up the war for his people as the factions multiply, carrying the old covenant of blood out of the ruined mansion and into the militias of the street.
suggested_refs: Video of the capture of Samuel Doe, September 1990

segments.name: The Naked Brigade, the warlord bulletproof

stops.name: Monrovia, the raising of the Naked Base Commandos
stops.campa: He takes up arms with ULIMO and gathers his own militia: the Naked Base Commandos, the Butt Naked Brigade, dozens of fighters, many of them children as young as nine. Before battle he strips to nothing but shoes and charms, and leads his boys naked into the guns. The nakedness is the covenant: bare before the enemy, protected by the rites, he believes no bullet can touch him. The child-soldiers follow the naked general into the fire, fed on the old sacrifices and on cocaine, and the city learns to fear the sight of him.
suggested_refs: Photographs of General Butt Naked leading fighters, Monrovia 1996

stops.name: The splitting of ULIMO, under Roosevelt Johnson
stops.campa: The movement breaks in two: ULIMO-J of Roosevelt Johnson against ULIMO-K of Alhaji Kromah, and the naked general throws his brigade behind Johnson. Faction turns on faction and the war grows more intricate and more cruel; alliances shift like the tide over Bushrod. Through it all Blahyi keeps his rites, offering the sacrifices that he believes make his boys and himself proof against harm. He is a commander now within a warlord's coalition, his charms his armour, his child-soldiers his sword.
suggested_refs: Photographs of Liberian faction fighters, mid-1990s

stops.name: Bushrod Island & the port, the ground of the killing
stops.campa: Across Bushrod Island and the Freeport, over the bridges of the Mesurado, the brigade fights and burns. Here the general marches his naked column through the ruined streets, an assault rifle in one hand and a trophy of the dead in the other. He orders the sacrifice of a child before combat, that the god may grant the day; he pours blood and eats heart as the elders taught him. The island port, the artery of the capital, becomes an altar the length of a battlefield.

stops.name: Duala Market, New Kru Town: the general's ground
stops.campa: About the great market of Duala in New Kru Town, the busiest quarter of the north city, the naked brigade holds and fights. In peacetime this is the wholesale heart of Monrovia; in the war it is checkpoint and killing-ground. The boy-commandos, high and armed, man the roads; the general walks among them clothed only in fetish and shoe, and the market people vanish before him. Later he will walk these same streets weeping, a Bible in his hand, to beg the pardon of the living.
suggested_refs: Duala Market, New Kru Town, Monrovia

stops.name: Po River bridge, the northwestern gate
stops.campa: At the Po River bridge on the northwestern edge of the city, the war's tide breaks back and forth. The bridge is a threshold of the capital: hold it and you hold the road in. Here too the naked general ranges with his commandos, believing the rites of the grove make him a wall no fire can breach. The river runs beneath the fighting; the covenant of blood holds him, he thinks, invincible, and the offerings continue, month by month, life by life.

stops.name: Central Monrovia, the battle of April 6
stops.campa: On the sixth of April the city convulses. Factions move to seize Roosevelt Johnson and Monrovia erupts into open war street by street. In the roar of it a witness sees the general atop a truck, an assault rifle in one hand and the severed genitals of a man in the other. Hundreds die before the guns fall silent. This day alone he will name to the Commission when he reckons his dead. The slaughter reaches its summit, and the summit is where the light will find him.
suggested_refs: Photographs of the April 1996 battle of Monrovia

segments.name: The Road to Damascus, the light on the battlefield

stops.name: The battlefield outside Monrovia, the vision of the Man of light
stops.campa: In July, on the field, after a sacrifice, the light comes. A Man stands before him swathed in blinding brightness and speaks in his own tongue: he is a slave to Satan, and he will die. Repent and live, or refuse and die. The naked general, who has believed himself bulletproof, a god's own instrument, is struck through with terror. He knows the voice for Christ. The covenant of the grove shatters in an instant. He will say this is his last day upon the battlefield; the warrior of the devil is undone by a single sentence of light.
stops.quote: Repent and live, or refuse and die.
stops.quote_source: Blahyi's account of the July 1996 vision (autobiography; retold in interviews and TRC testimony)
suggested_refs: The Redemption of General Butt Naked (2011)
Caravaggio, Conversion of Saint Paul (parallel image of the light on the road)

stops.name: A Monrovia church, laying down the arms
stops.campa: He abandons his unit and his guns and flees to a church, where he begins to sleep among the pews. To his ULIMO commanders he sends word that he serves another now: his new Commander is Jesus Christ. The congregation gathers over him to pray the demonic power out of his body; a bishop's church, it is said, fasts fifty-four days for his deliverance. The general who feared no bullet now trembles before God, weeping in a church, waiting to be washed of the grove.
stops.quote: My new Commander is Jesus Christ.
stops.quote_source: Blahyi to his ULIMO-J superiors, 1996 (retold in interviews and autobiography)

stops.name: The streets of Monrovia, the cassette preacher
stops.campa: As the war ends and Charles Taylor is voted into the mansion, the delivered general takes to the streets as an open-air preacher, hawking recorded sermons from a cassette. The city that fled him now hears his voice raised not in a war-cry but in an altar-call. His whole gospel is himself: if God could reach the naked general, God can reach anyone. Yet the new President's men eye him with suspicion, and the ground grows unsafe; the preacher of the pavement will soon have to flee the land.
stops.quote: If God can save me, He can save you, too.
stops.quote_source: Blahyi's street-preaching message, Monrovia c.1997 (interviews; sermon cassettes)

stops.name: Buduburam camp, Ghana: confession in the refugee church
stops.campa: He crosses out of Liberia to the Buduburam refugee camp west of Accra, among the tens of thousands of Liberians scattered by the war. In a camp church he makes his confession and, he says, has his life saved. Here in the wilderness of exile the warlord is unmade and the evangelist is born; the sermons begin, the calling hardens. Away from the country that fears and hates him, in the dust of a camp of the displaced, the servant of the devil is remade a servant of Christ.
stops.quote: If God can save me, He can save you, too.

stops.name: Buduburam, the founding of End Time Train
stops.campa: In exile he founds his ministry, End Time Train Evangelistic Ministries, and takes up the road of the preacher. The train of the last days, he calls it, gathering the lost before the end. From the camp he begins the long labor of return: he will go back to help disarm the fighters, then withdraw again to Ghana, then come home for good. The wilderness years shape the man who will one day stand before his nation and name every death he caused.
suggested_refs: End Time Train Evangelistic Ministries Inc.

segments.name: The Return and the Confession, before the nation

stops.name: Monrovia, the disarmament of the fighters
stops.campa: With Taylor gone into exile and the guns at last laid down, Blahyi comes home from Ghana to work the disarmament: turning fighters, some of them his own former boys, out of the bush and toward the programmes of peace. For a year he labours at it before returning again to the camp. The general who once armed children now works to unmake soldiers; the evangelist walks back into the country that fears his name, testing whether the man of the pulpit can be trusted on the ground where the man of the grove once ruled.

stops.name: Centennial Memorial Pavilion, Monrovia: the Truth and Reconciliation Commission
stops.campa: He comes home and stands before the Truth and Reconciliation Commission at the Centennial Memorial Pavilion, the first Liberian warlord to face it. Broadcast live across the country on radio and television, he confesses the killings, orders of rape, the sacrifices of children. Reckoning April sixth and all the war and every evil, he says the dead are not less than twenty thousand. He does not plead innocence. He says he is a hundred percent guilty; that those who will not forgive him are right not to; that he is willing to be tried, even at The Hague.
stops.quote: I'm 100 percent guilty for all the things I did in the past. They are right not to forgive me.
stops.quote_source: Joshua Blahyi, testimony before the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Liberia, Monrovia, January 2008
suggested_refs: TRC of Liberia testimony video, 15 January 2008
Centennial Memorial Pavilion, Ashmun Street, Monrovia

stops.name: The villages of the dead, begging forgiveness
stops.campa: After the confession comes the harder road. He goes out from the city into the villages and towns where his brigade killed, seeking the families of the dead to beg their pardon face to face. Some drive him off; some, out of Christian faith or out of a weary sense that forgiveness is the only way the country can go forward, take his hand. The documentary follows him for five years down these roads of the wronged: the general who was bulletproof now defenceless, offering only his confession and his tears.
suggested_refs: The Redemption of General Butt Naked (2011), dir. Eric Strauss & Daniele Anastasion

segments.name: The Pulpit, the preacher of today

stops.name: The rehabilitation camp, the gathering of the boy-soldiers
stops.campa: Through Journeys Against Violence he gathers to himself the young men who were once fighters, some his own former commandos, feeding, housing and preaching to the ruined children of the war he helped to wage. He calls it his penance and his mission at once: to answer the boys he ruined by trying to raise them up. Critics say the camp is a shield against prosecution; he answers that he has confessed everything and is ready to be judged. The naked general herds the sons of the war toward a peace he denied their childhood.
suggested_refs: The Redemption of General Butt Naked (2011)

stops.name: Paynesville / Monrovia, the pastor of the present
stops.campa: Today he stands in the pulpit, president of End Time Train, an evangelist and pastor on the edge of the capital. He preaches the man he was as the proof of the God he serves: if grace could reach the naked general who ate the hearts of children, no soul is past saving. His enemies call the conversion a shelter from the courts; he answers that he has already confessed all and would stand trial. The living journey runs on, close to the present: the slave of Satan grown grey in the service of Christ.
stops.quote: If God can save me, He can save you, too.
stops.quote_source: Blahyi's recurring preaching message (interviews; sermon recordings)
suggested_refs: End Time Train Evangelistic Ministries, Liberia
Interviews and sermons of Pastor Joshua Milton Blahyi
